rice-white-cooked-no-added-fat.title: Rice, white, cooked, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: White rice, cooked without added fat, is a fully prepared grain product obtained from polished white rice after boiling in water without oil or other fats. It has a soft texture, neutral flavor, and is commonly used as a base side dish or ingredient in a variety of meals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: White rice is the most widely consumed type of rice worldwide.
Cooked white rice without added fat provides about 130 kcal per 100 g.
It is easily digestible and often recommended in diets aimed at gastrointestinal recovery.
Compared to whole brown rice, white rice has a longer shelf life due to removal of bran and germ.
In Japan, rice is a cultural symbol and is frequently served as a simple boiled side.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Starch carbohydrates are quickly converted to glucose, providing the body with a rapid source of energy.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The absence of added fats makes it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Rice contains thiamine (B1), niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: It provides magnesium, phosphorus and small amounts of iron, supporting muscle and bone function.

items.title: Hypoallergenic
items.content: Rice rarely triggers allergic reactions, making it safe for most people.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: White rice raises blood sugar quickly, so individuals with diabetes should monitor portion sizes.

items.title: Low fiber content
items.content: Compared with whole grains, cooked white rice contains little dietary fiber, which may affect digestion.

items.title: Arsenic presence
items.content: In some regions rice can contain trace arsenic; rinsing the rice before cooking is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Rice can be served as a standalone side, added to soups, salads, pilafs, sushi, or used as a base for risotto. For flavor variety, combine it with herbs, spices, vegetables, or lean protein.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked rice in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 4‑5 days. For longer storage, freeze portions in bags at –18 °C, where it retains quality for up to 3 months. Reheat thoroughly before consumption.

content.title: About
content.content: Bean soup is a hearty dish made from cooked beans, vegetables, spices, and sometimes meat. Beans are rich in protein, fiber, and complex carbohydrates, making this soup a filling meal for lunch or dinner.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Beans are one of the oldest cultivated crops, grown for over 7,000 years.
There are more than 700 bean varieties, differing in size, color, and flavor.
Bean soup appears in traditional dishes worldwide: Mexican chili, Russian bean stew, and Indian dal.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Beans provide plant‑based protein that supports muscle maintenance and tissue repair.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Dietary fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Source of iron and magnesium
items.content: These minerals are essential for hemoglobin formation and nervous system function.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Bean soup raises blood glucose slowly, which is beneficial for people with pre‑diabetes.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Beans contain flavonoids and polyphenols that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Phytic acid
items.content: Raw beans contain phytic acid, which can reduce mineral absorption; soaking and thorough cooking are recommended.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to legumes.

items.title: Gas formation
items.content: Beans contain oligosaccharides that can cause flatulence in sensitive people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve bean soup hot, often garnished with herbs, sour cream, or crusty bread. It can be prepared vegetarian with only vegetables, or with meat such as sausage, ham, or chicken.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cooked soup in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze it in portion‑sized bags for up to 3 months.
